output.proposal: HB No. 11288 seeks to create additional divisions in the Court of Appeals, increasing them from seventeen (17) to twenty-six (26) and the number of Court of Appeals Justices from sixty-nine (69) to seventy-eight (78), and to set permanent stations for the divisions in the Cities of Manila, Cebu, Cagayan de Oro, Vigan and Davao, by amending Batas Pambansa Blg. 129 (Judiciary Reorganization Act of 1980), as amended.
output.alignment: The measure does not create a new body but expands an existing court of the Judiciary; the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), which covers the streamlining of the Executive branch, is therefore of limited direct application, and the review should instead assess the justification for nine (9) additional Justices and divisions (e.g., case load and regional distribution of cases), the consistency of the amended Sections 3, 4 and 10 of BP Blg. 129, and the personnel, facilities and operating requirements of the new divisions and stations. No matching FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item was identified.
legislative_history: HB No. 11288 was filed on September 14, 2026 by Representative Eric G. Yap; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available records.
A bill with the same title, HB No. 1449, was filed earlier in the 20th Congress on July 7, 2025 and is pending in the Committee (title match only; text not reviewed).

Bills with matching titles were filed in the 19th Congress (HB Nos. 4033, 4302, 4702, 4959 and 5219, and SB No. 1186) and in the 18th Congress (HB Nos. 4323, 6819 and 7001, and SB No. 1253), all recorded as pending in the Committee (title match only; text not reviewed).

Narrower proposals on the Court of Appeals were also filed: HB No. 5868 (18th Congress) on two additional divisions in Davao City, and HB No. 7513 (19th Congress) on an additional division in the City of Baguio.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11288 seeks to expand the Court of Appeals by creating additional divisions and increasing the number of its Justices from sixty-nine (69) to seventy-eight (78). Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 1 (Amendment of Section 3 of BP Blg. 129) provides that the Court of Appeals shall consist of a Presiding Justice and seventy-seven (77) Associate Justices appointed by the President, with precedence based on the dates of appointment.
b. Section 2 (Amendment of Section 4 of BP Blg. 129) provides that the Court shall exercise its powers through twenty-six (26) divisions of three (3) members each, up from seventeen (17), and may sit en banc for non-adjudicatory functions.
c. Section 3 (Amendment of Section 10 of BP Blg. 129) provides permanent stations for the divisions: the first seventeen (17) in the City of Manila; the 18th to 20th in the City of Cebu; the 21st to 23rd in the City of Cagayan de Oro; the 24th in the City of Vigan; and the 25th and 26th in the City of Davao, each for cases from specified judicial regions, and allows the Supreme Court to authorize any division to hold sessions elsewhere when justified by public interest or case load.
d. Section 4 (Referral of Pending Cases) provides that, upon effectivity, pending cases not yet submitted for resolution shall be referred to the proper division.
e. Section 5 (Transfer of Assignment) provides that no member may be transferred to another station without written consent, except for temporary assignment, and that the Act shall not affect security of tenure or seniority.
f. Section 6 (Funding) provides that the amounts needed shall be included in the General Appropriations Act of the year following enactment and thereafter.
g. Sections 7 (Separability Clause), 8 (Repealing Clause) and 9 (Effectivity) provide the standard final clauses, with effectivity fifteen (15) days after publication in two (2) newspapers of general circulation.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11288 may be considered alongside HB No. 1449 of the 20th Congress, which bears the same title, and the identically titled measures of the 18th and 19th Congresses, as well as the narrower proposals for additional divisions in Davao City (HB No. 5868, 18th Congress) and in the City of Baguio (HB No. 7513, 19th Congress). It amends Sections 3, 4 and 10 of BP Blg. 129, as amended by Executive Order No. 33, s. 1986, and builds on the composition set by RA No. 8246. No matching FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item was identified. The review should assess the case-load justification for the nine (9) additional Justices and divisions, the cost of the associated personnel, chambers and stations, and whether the Judiciary's existing appropriations can absorb the initial requirement before the General Appropriations Act provides for it under Section 6 (Funding).
